interactions.summary: Jiang closes the morning discussion by arguing that Virgil changes theory to justify prior action and that sin means being unable to forgive oneself enough to admit error.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang monologue with one student completion.

interactions.summary: After lunch, Francois presents a map of consciousness moving between outer ego/materiality and inner love, and Jiang affirms it, adds angels-and-demons ambience, cites Rupert Sheldrake, and sets up an experiment.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Francois presentation followed by Jiang response and experimental instructions.

speaker_notes.note: This fragment is a student's verbal completion of Jiang's point that Virgil is weighed down by past actions.

claims.claim: Jiang says people revise worldview to justify past action rather than simply admit they were wrong, and he applies this to Virgil's imperial poem and self-justification.
Jiang defines sin here as being weighed down by one's own actions and refusing the self-forgiveness that would allow one to change.
Francois presents consciousness as a movable field ranging from an outer zone of money, time, fear, ego, and materiality to an inner zone of love, hope, and family.
Jiang validates the presentation enough to connect it to William James, to the Divine Comedy's angelic and demonic ambience, and to Rupert Sheldrake's ideas.

signature_moments.moment: Hell is described as self-incarceration produced by refusing to forgive your own past actions.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you just basically put yourself in hell for all eternity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns sin from rule-breaking into a dynamic of self-judgment and frozen identity.

signature_moments.moment: Consciousness is pictured as a circle that can drift outward toward material fear or inward toward love and hope, with angels and demons nudging the movement.
signature_moments.source_phrase: source in the middle ... exterior ... present material and ego ... angels are more meant to push us inward and demons outward
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is a vivid mid-lecture model linking moral psychology, cosmology, and reading practice.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Francois invokes Rupert Sheldrake's term for shared patterns or fields that shape how consciousness converges.

chronology_notes.note: This packet marks a same-day shift from Virgil's self-justifying sin model into a student-led consciousness map that Jiang partially endorses and extends with Sheldrake-style field language.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR around Francois's opening remarks is rough, but the present/material outer ring versus inner love/hope structure is still recoverable from the full turn.
